A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HART/AP-GRPO work, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, both end with references: the cited Appendices A–E in v1 and A–F in v3 are absent, limiting comparison of proofs, training details and supplementary analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original HART benchmark results, grounding experiments, component ablations and qualitative comparisons in Sections 4–5.

after.justification: v3 retains original HART results and reports additional benchmark, backbone, grounding and training-order experiments.

M1.justification: The documented procedure remains ROI prediction, cropped-region-only answering during AP-GRPO, followed by SFT with the full image visible. The AP-GRPO objective and dynamic weights in Equations 4–6 are unchanged. Testing additional backbones does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: v3 adds Visual CoT grounding evaluation, BLINK and Mantis-Eval multi-image tasks, and MathVista mathematical visual reasoning. The original MME-RealWorld, TreeBench, MMStar, V* and HR-Bench coverage remains. This substantially broadens the evaluated inputs and task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add GRPO + SFT and MGPO + SFT comparisons. Table 4 adds InternVL3-8B and LLaVA-OneVision-7B to the retained benchmark comparisons previously restricted to Qwen2.5-VL-7B and HART. Conversely, SFT-only is removed from the TreeBench answer and grounding comparisons.

E3.justification: The pilot changes from TreeBench with IoU to 4,042 filtered Visual CoT questions, excluding complex/descriptive and yes/no answers and comparing joint answer/grounding outcomes with and without HART. Tabulated grounding evaluation switches from IoU to intersection over ground-truth at threshold 0.3. Table 5 also introduces HART post-training on InternVL3-8B.

E4.justification: v3 Table 1 directly tests how withholding the full image changes answer–grounding agreement, whereas v1 only diagnoses baseline errors. Table 7 adds SFT-before-AP-GRPO versus AP-GRPO-before-SFT, revises the component controls and retains the positive-k sensitivity tests. Figure 4 supplies two additional qualitative comparisons. Further claimed appendix analyses cannot be inspected.

E5.justification: Neither main text reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The referenced training and supplementary-experiment appendices are missing from both PDFs, preventing a reliable comparison of statistical reporting there.

E6.justification: HART's headline accuracies remain 62.4% on MME-RealWorld-Lite and 43.7% on TreeBench, but many results are added or revised. New HART scores include 56.8 on BLINK, 72.8 on Mantis-Eval and 71.8 on MathVista. Table 2 changes MGPO's overall score from 60.5 to 55.1 despite retaining its subtask scores. The grounding figures of 46.9% in v1 and 75.4% in v3 use different metrics and are labeled HART and AP-GRPO respectively, so they are not a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Proposition 2 adds an existential alpha in [0,1] multiplying the erroneous-grounding gradient term in Equation 7. This weakens v1's claim of complete subtraction to potentially partial suppression. Proposition 1 remains unchanged; the referenced proofs are unavailable in both PDFs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the prominent claim that 7B HART surpasses 72B models with named benchmark coverage and improvements over the base model. The central contributions—annotation-free grounding, the closed loop, AP-GRPO and strong benchmark performance—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 qualify v1's implication that correct answers establish faithful grounding: v3 says they are more likely to indicate it and reports residual incorrect grounding. The ground-truth-gradient interpretation following Proposition 2 is removed. v3 also drops the explicit future-work paragraph discussing model scale, dataset scale and inference speed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a planned HART code-release destination, discloses that reinforcement fine-tuning comparisons share training data, and supplies per-task sample counts in Tables 2–3. Table 4 removes the earlier numerical image-resolution column. Detailed training settings and newly mentioned costs remain inaccessible because Appendix C is absent; the code statement does not establish release availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for BLINK, Mantis, MathVista and two grounding-metric references, while removing the works on closing the GPT-4V gap and scaling vision pre-training to 4K. Section 2.1 changes its critique of prior approaches from training/thinking cost to overlooking grounding. The main annotation-free versus annotation-supervised positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, updates affiliations and corresponding-author information, edits the abstract and selected explanatory passages, adds acknowledgements and removes the separate Experimental Settings heading. Most prose and the overall introduction–related work–preliminaries–method–experiments–conclusion sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a narrower single-column layout, substantially resizing figures and tables. Table 1 becomes a joint-outcome display; Tables 2–3 reorder columns and add sample counts and second-best markings; Table 4 expands; and a backbone-comparison table is introduced. Figure 3 gains an aggregate panel, and Figure 4 expands from one example to three.

improvement.justification: The added two-stage baseline comparisons, direct ROI-only diagnostic and additional-backbone results strengthen the evidence supporting the unchanged method. More cautious grounding interpretations and the corrected MGPO aggregate also improve credibility. These gains are limited by unavailable appendices, the grounding-metric change, and an unresolved inconsistency: v3 Table 7 retains GRPO ablation scores that do not aggregate to its revised main-table results. The supplied material supports a limited net improvement in evidential quality.
